excerpt: Typeahead is AI autocomplete for every text field on a Mac, run by a local model so writing stays on your device. $96/year or $149 lifetime.
content:
Typeahead suggests the rest of what you are typing in almost any Mac app, as grey text at your cursor. Press Tab to accept the whole suggestion, the right arrow for one word, or Esc to dismiss it. It works in Mail, Slack, Notion, Messages, Notes, Word, Obsidian and browsers, and is switched off in password fields, password managers and finance apps. You can set a writing style per app, such as professional in Mail and friendly in Slack, or describe your own in plain English, and it learns phrases you use often. You can review or delete what it has learned.

Suggestions come from a model that runs on your Mac: Gemma or Qwen, downloaded once, or your own GGUF model file. The company says your writing never leaves the Mac and the app has no telemetry; it reads nearby text through macOS Accessibility, needs no account, and works offline after setup. It needs macOS 14 or later, 8 GB of memory and about 4 GB of free space.

Typeahead is made by Noats Inc., whose terms are governed by California law. It costs $96 a year or $10 a month after a 14-day trial, or $149 once for a lifetime licence.

Typeahead launched on Product Hunt on 6 July 2026 and finished #2 for the day, with 421 upvotes and 74 comments. It has 6 Product Hunt reviews averaging 4.83 out of 5 (as of 14 October 2026).

We have not tested Typeahead ourselves. This page brings together its official site, pricing page, terms and privacy policy, its Product Hunt listing and the official pages of comparable apps, and says where each fact comes from.

profile.os: macOS 14 or later, 8 GB of memory, about 4 GB free space
profile.summary_short: AI autocomplete for every Mac app, run on a local model
use_cases: Finishing emails and chat replies faster in any Mac app
Keeping a different tone per app, such as formal in Mail and casual in Slack
Reusing phrases you type often without a snippet tool
Using AI suggestions where cloud tools are not allowed for privacy reasons

fit: type a lot on a Mac across many apps
want AI help that keeps your text on your own machine
prefer paying once over a subscription
not_fit: use Windows, Linux, iPhone or iPad: it is a Mac app only
have a Mac with less than 8 GB of memory or macOS older than 14
want AI to draft whole messages for you: it completes what you are already writing

alternatives.intro: Another local Mac autocomplete app, the suggestions built into macOS, and the best-known AI writing assistant. Prices come from each product's own pages, checked on 14 October 2026.

items.name: Cotypist
items.what: Mac app that predicts your next words in most apps, processed locally
items.starts_at: Free for 100 completed words a day; see its site for Plus and Pro
items.difference: Very similar idea with a free daily allowance; it needs an Apple silicon Mac.

items.name: macOS predictive text
items.what: Inline word and phrase suggestions built into macOS
items.difference: Free and built in, but completes words and short phrases rather than whole sentences in your style.

items.name: Grammarly
items.what: AI writing assistant that checks and rewrites text across apps
items.starts_at: Free plan; see its pricing page for paid plans
items.difference: Checks and rewrites text using cloud AI rather than suggesting the next words locally as you type.

faq.a: A Mac app that shows AI suggestions for the rest of your sentence in almost any text field; press Tab to accept.

faq.q: Does my writing leave my Mac?
faq.a: The company says no: suggestions come from a local model, and the app has no telemetry. Network use is for licence checks, updates and model downloads. Its website's separate AI tools do send text to Google's Gemini API.
$96 a year or $10 a month after a 14-day free trial, or $149 once for a lifetime licence. Subscriptions cover up to 3 Macs; lifetime covers all your Macs.
macOS 14 or later, 8 GB of memory and about 4 GB of free space.

faq.q: How is it different from Grammarly or ChatGPT?
faq.a: Those check or draft text separately; Typeahead suggests the next words in place as you type, in your own style.
Yes, within 30 days of your first payment on any plan, by emailing the company. Renewals are not covered.

faq.q: What are the alternatives to Typeahead?
faq.a: Cotypist is a similar local Mac autocomplete app with a free daily allowance; macOS has basic predictive text built in; Grammarly is a cloud writing assistant.
